label: Benefit Card
title: Benefit Card
summary: Use a Benefit Card to list what a plan or offer gives, with an optional upsell and one button to upgrade.
corePrinciple: Show what people get, then one way to get it.

anatomy.title: What you earn, what you get, one button
anatomy.description: A white card with a header of earnings rows and a divider, an upsell line, a list of benefits, and an upgrade button, 8 px apart.

states.title: A summary with or without an action
states.description: The card has no state of its own: only its button acts, through onButtonPress, with Button's usual states. onPress makes the header a button named by its title, and pressing the header or the lists dims them and calls it; the upsell and the card’s button stay separate buttons beside it.

sizing.title: 344 px wide, as tall as its content
sizing.description: It's 344 px wide unless you set width to another number or a percentage, such as 100% to fill its container. It has 12 px padding, 12 px corners, and 8 px between sections, and it's as tall as what it shows. Figma's card is 344 × 221.

content.title: A label, short perks, and figures
content.description: Write the header title as a label, such as “You will earn”. Keep each row to a short noun phrase and put its number in trailingText, where the figures line up on the right. Label the button with a verb, such as “Upgrade”.

inContext.description: The plan screen fills its width with the card (width 100%) and starts checkout when people press Upgrade, through onButtonPress. The card doesn't act on its own.

sources.title: Use the public Benefit Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (16 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s BenefitCard is one 344 × 221 component with header and Button switches and two list slots; its upsell is the retired Nudge, with 12 px text and no close button. In this build the upsell has 14 px text and, since the #271 fix, no Close button, as in Figma; the card is 223 px tall, 2 more than Figma. The header swaps Figma’s spacing: 4 px under the title and 8 px between rows, 8 and 4 in Figma. The card and its title stay white and black in every mode. Its default rows repeat one placeholder, so always pass your own. The published Storybook still shows the old page and the older nudge.
